correctness.rationale: The root polytope is exactly the 4-cube intersected with the L1 ball of radius 2; its 24 octahedral facets at distance 1 give volume 8. For five roots on the radius-sqrt(2) sphere, the augmented Gram identity D²=5 det(G) and trace(G)≤10 give |D|≤25 sqrt(5)/4<14. The D4 even-coordinate-sum condition makes D an even integer, hence |D|≤12. The explicit five-root witness has determinant 12 and simplex volume 1/2. A standalone exhaustive exact census of C(24,5)=42504 sets checks that exactly 48 achieve 12, all in one B4 orbit, none sharing four vertices, and all with edge-square spectrum {4 sixfold,6 fourfold}; independent cofactor and permutation determinant implementations agree on every input. Multiaffine vertex reduction handles arbitrary contained simplices, and the nonshared-four-face property rules out any optimizer having a nonvertex point. Finite enumeration is used solely for an exhaustively finite subset classification, not as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 24-cell is the exceptional regular self-dual 4-polytope and canonical D4 root convex hull. Its normalized largest-simplex volume is a natural affine-invariant extremal quantity, with a complete nonregular equality classification rather than a selected numerical example. The root-lattice parity mechanism and a full rigidity proof distinguish the result from the known universal sphere optimum or a routine determinant substitution. The exact 1/16 ratio and 48-element orbit give a reusable benchmark for inscribed-polytope extremal and root-configuration geometry, without asserting a general-d theorem.
